pharm: Fluoroquinolone; inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV
quick: With or without food; avoid cations
Category C; only if benefit > risk
summary: Ofloxacin is an oral fluoroquinolone antibiotic for respiratory, urinary, skin, prostate, and genital infections. It carries a boxed warning for disabling, potentially irreversible reactions (tendinitis/rupture, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects) and can worsen myasthenia gravis. Reserve for chronic bronchitis exacerbation and uncomplicated cystitis only when no alternatives exist.
indications: Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis (when no alternative)

dosage.d: Half usual unit dose every 24 h

admin: Do not take antacids (Ca/Mg/Al), sucralfate, iron, zinc multivitamins, or didanosine within 2 hours before or after a dose
Discontinue immediately at first sign of tendon pain, neuropathy, or serious CNS reaction
Reserve for infections without alternative treatment options where indicated
moa: Inhibits bacterial topoisomerase II (DNA gyrase) and topoisomerase IV, blocking DNA replication, transcription, repair, and recombination, producing bactericidal activity.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to ofloxacin or any quinolone
Known history of myasthenia gravis (may exacerbate weakness)
relative: History of tendon disorders/rupture with fluoroquinolones
Age >60, corticosteroid use, or organ transplant (tendon-rupture risk)

preg: Category C; use only if benefit justifies fetal risk
lact: Excreted in milk at plasma-like levels; decide to stop nursing or drug
renal: CrCl 20-50: usual dose every 24 h; CrCl <20: half dose every 24 h
hepatic: Severe liver disease (cirrhosis): do not exceed 400 mg/day

major: Antacids/sucralfate/iron/zinc/didanosine (chelation lowers absorption - separate by 2 h)
Class IA/III antiarrhythmics and QT-prolonging drugs (torsade risk)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; avoid dairy/cation-containing products near dosing
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; may worsen CNS adverse effects
interactions.diagnostics: Use caution interpreting glucose tests; monitor for dysglycemia

emergency: Anaphylaxis / severe hypersensitivity (can follow first dose; airway support, epinephrine)
Tendon rupture - stop drug, rest affected limb
Disabling peripheral neuropathy or CNS reaction - discontinue immediately
Myasthenia gravis exacerbation with breathing difficulty
Aortic aneurysm or dissection - sudden chest/back/abdominal pain

monitoring: Tendon pain/inflammation during and for months after therapy
QT interval / electrolytes with risk factors
Theophylline levels and INR (warfarin) when co-administered
Renal and hepatic function in impairment
counsel: Stop the drug and call your provider at the first sign of tendon pain, swelling, or rupture; rest the limb
Report numbness, tingling, or weakness (possible nerve damage)
Report new anxiety, confusion, hallucinations, or seizures
Avoid antacids, iron, zinc, and dairy within 2 hours of your dose
Avoid excessive sun; use sun protection (photosensitivity)
pearls: BOXED WARNING: disabling, potentially irreversible reactions (tendinitis/tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects) can occur together; discontinue immediately if any appear
Avoid in known myasthenia gravis - fluoroquinolones can worsen muscle weakness
Class fluoroquinolone risk also includes aortic aneurysm/dissection - report sudden chest/back/abdominal pain
Reserve for chronic bronchitis exacerbation and uncomplicated cystitis only when no alternative exists
Chelates with di/trivalent cations - separate antacids, iron, zinc, and didanosine by 2 hours
Inhibits CYP and raises theophylline/warfarin levels; QT-prolonging risk with antiarrhythmics
missed: Take when remembered; skip if near next dose, do not double
overdose: CNS effects (drowsiness, dizziness, disorientation, slurred speech), nausea; empty stomach, hydrate, supportive care; not well removed by dialysis
refs: U.S. FDA label via openFDA / DailyMed
